en: So
what are search algorithms and why might we
need them? It's quite common in programming
that you're confronted with lists of data,
with an array of data that can be an array
of numbers like it is on this slide, but it
can of course be an array with any kind of
data. Doesn't have to be numbers. It can be
strings, it can be objects, anything like
that. But I'll focus on number arrays here
because that's easiest and makes
understanding these algorithms easier as
well. Generally, you can work with any
arrays though.
Now, in such an array of data, you might be
looking for a certain element. Let's say
we're looking for the number 5.
And then you need, well, an algorithm, you
need some logic that in the end makes sure
that if you're looking for a certain
element, that element is found. Found and
retrieved from the array,
or you're getting an error message or some
dummy return value if the element is not
found.
Now you can actually use different
algorithms for different kinds of lists,
and these different algorithms also have
different time complexities.
And there are 2 essential algorithms, and
these are the algorithms we're going to have
a look at in this module.
